statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail risk remains in the low band with no live Nasdaq-100 price path available inside the weekend futures halt, while stress-side conditions stay high on the unresolved Strait of Hormuz disruption, elevated crude and rising global long yields.
recommendation: Tail remains below the block threshold, so the deterministic mapping returns EA_ON for both NQ futures and NAS100 CFD. A narrow observation window is flagged around the scheduled Sunday CME restart, where thin liquidity and two-sided weekend headline risk are concentrated. Existing-position management and emergency protection logic are unaffected by this mapping.
headline: Nasdaq-100 futures still halted about an hour before the scheduled Sunday CME restart; tail low, stress high on unresolved Hormuz disruption
body:
No live Nasdaq-100 price path exists at this timestamp. CME equity index futures remain inside the weekend halt and are scheduled to restart near 22:00 UTC, roughly an hour after this assessment, so the evaluation continues to rest on the last completed cash session, verified cross-asset levels and the current macro and geopolitical backdrop rather than on observed intraday structure.

The September Nasdaq-100 futures contract last traded at 30,141.75, down 0.15% on Friday inside a 30,028.50-30,283.00 range on 397,964 contracts, and the cash index closed at 30,046.14, about 2.3% below its 30,762.20 52-week high while still finishing the week higher. VIX ended at 14.25, down 2.60% on the day, and Treasury constant-maturity yields stood at 4.15% for the 2Y, 4.63% for the 10Y and 5.21% for the 30Y at the latest H.15 publication, against a broader theme of rising long rates globally. Subdued implied volatility alongside a contained settlement range is not the profile of a market already in one-way structure.

This hour's checks found no new escalation beyond what was already reflected, and no change in any verified level. The dominant unresolved channel is still energy and geopolitics. The Strait of Hormuz remains effectively disrupted with the U.S. naval blockade in place; documented August incidents include a bulk carrier struck on 3 August, an ADNOC tanker hit on 8 August and two ADNOC tankers attacked by unmanned aerial vehicles on 13 August. Iran has moved to condition transit on passage permits and tolls of up to 7% of cargo value, terms Washington has rejected while signalling that the blockade could continue indefinitely. WTI settled near $82.40 (+1.42%) and Brent near $88.52 (+1.67%), extending the week's advance beyond 5%, while positioning data showed speculative oil length shrinking for a second consecutive week. That combination of firm prices and thinning bullish bets is why the restart is scored as a stress and gap concentration point rather than as directional tail evidence.

No observed amplifier stack is present: there is no measurable retracement behaviour, no session extremes to hold and no opening structure to score while the market is closed. Under the fixed mapping the current tail of 15 keeps the mapped policy state at EA_ON. The week ahead is macro-light into midweek, with the Empire State survey and the NAHB index on Monday, FOMC minutes on 19 August the first high-impact scheduled catalyst and flash PMIs on 21 August the second, alongside a heavy large-cap retail earnings slate from Tuesday onward. The Kansas City Fed symposium falls on 27-29 August, outside this seven-day window.

Tail moved narrowly between 12 and 17, stress climbed from the mid-60s into the low 80s before easing back toward 70, and confidence ranged from 65 to 80. The entire window falls inside the cash-market weekend and the CME futures halt, so that trajectory reflects an accumulating energy and geopolitical backdrop rather than any observed Nasdaq-100 price structure.
outlookSummary: The scheduled CME restart near 22:00 UTC carries the highest conditional tail of the forecast at 18, reflecting thin liquidity and a two-sided Hormuz headline set rather than observed structure. Asian and European hours are expected to normalise toward 13-14 if the reopening print is orderly. A secondary rise to 17 is carried across the Monday U.S. cash open at 13:30 UTC and the first hour after it, where opening-auction continuation with shallow pullbacks would be the first genuine tail evidence of the new week. All forecast hours stay below the 20 threshold, so the mapping remains EA_ON throughout on current evidence; a disorderly reopening gap or repeated extension after failed retracements would invalidate that path.
